body:
When generating text, top-k filtering keeps only the $k$ highest probability tokens and sets the rest to zero. To ensure probabilities still sum to one, the remaining values are divided by their new sum.

Look at the bar chart to see how the relative heights change between the full softmax and the renormalized top-k distributions.


Because of this division, the reported probability of the chosen token increases. Its new value is scaled up by dividing by the sum of the top-$k$ probabilities.

This means the model's confidence score reported in logs differs from the raw softmax output.

title: Top-k filtering and reported token probabilities
body:
When generating text, language models assign probabilities to every vocabulary token using the softmax function.

Applying top-k filtering discards all tokens except the $k$ highest-scoring ones, restricting the choice set before sampling occurs.

```rh-diagram
{"version":1,"diagram":{"title":"Full softmax and top-3 sampling","caption":"The kept tokens hold 80% of the probability. Divide each kept probability by that total.","kind":"bar-chart","unit":"%","variant":"grouped","categories":["A","B","C","D","E"],"series":[{"label":"Full softmax","values":[50,30,10,6,4]},{"label":"Top-3 renormalized","values":[55.6,33.3,11.1,0,0]}]}}
```

To ensure the remaining probabilities sum to one, the model rescales the surviving values by dividing each by the sum of the kept probabilities.

This renormalization step changes the relative and absolute probabilities of the chosen token compared to the original softmax distribution.

Consequently, the reported probability of the sampled token depends on whether it is logged before or after this truncation and rescaling process takes place.

title: Top-k filtering and token probabilities
body:
Top-k filtering alters model generation by keeping only the $k$ highest probability tokens and setting the rest to zero. Look at the chart to see how probabilities are rescaled among the surviving tokens.

```rh-diagram
{"version":1,"diagram":{"title":"Full softmax and top-3 sampling","caption":"The kept tokens originally hold 100% of the probability. Divide each kept probability by that total.","kind":"bar-chart","unit":"%","variant":"grouped","categories":["on","near","under"],"series":[{"label":"Full softmax","values":[50,30,20]},{"label":"Top-3 renormalized","values":[50,30,20]}]}}
```

When you discard the tail, the remaining probabilities no longer sum to one. To fix this, softmax output values are renormalized by dividing each by the new sum.

This division changes the reported probability of every chosen token.

Instead of the raw model confidence, you observe a conditional probability over the restricted subset. This step ensures valid sampling distributions while altering the final confidence scores.

title: Top-k filtering and probabilities
body:
When generating text, models compute a probability distribution over vocabulary tokens using the softmax function.

Applying top-k filtering keeps only the $k$ most likely choices and sets all other tokens to zero probability. Look at the bar heights in the chart to see how filtering removes low-ranked items entirely.

```rh-diagram
{"version":1,"diagram":{"title":"Full softmax and top-3 sampling","caption":"The kept tokens originally hold 70% of the probability. Divide each kept probability by that total.","kind":"bar-chart","unit":"%","variant":"grouped","categories":["cat","dog","fox","bat","owl"],"series":[{"label":"Full softmax","values":[38,32,20,7,3]},{"label":"Top-3 renormalized","values":[54.3,45.7,0,0,0]}]}}
```

To ensure the remaining probabilities sum to one, the kept values are renormalized by dividing by their sum. Because the denominator shrinks, the relative probability assigned to the chosen token increases.

This changes the final reported log probability of the sampled token compared to the raw softmax output.

title: Top-k Filtering and Token Probabilities
body:
When generating text, models compute raw scores that turn into a probability distribution via softmax.

Top-k filtering keeps only the top $k$ tokens and sets all other probabilities to zero, changing how likely the final choice appears.

```rh-diagram
{"version":1,"diagram":{"title":"Full softmax and top-3 sampling","caption":"The kept tokens originally hold 77% of the probability. Divide each kept probability by that total.","kind":"bar-chart","unit":"%","variant":"grouped","categories":["on","near","under"],"series":[{"label":"Full softmax","values":[53,16,8]},{"label":"Top-3 renormalized","values":[69,21,10]}]}}
```

To make valid probabilities again, the kept values are divided by their sum so they add up to one. This renormalization scales up every kept token's score, meaning the reported probability of the chosen token increases.

Therefore, logging the token probability after top-k filtering yields a higher value than the model originally assigned it before truncation.

prompt: What does predicting the mean give as a regression baseline?
title: Predicting the Mean as a Regression Baseline
body:
When building a regression model, we often compare our results against a simple constant. The mean baseline always predicts the average value of the target for every single input sample.

Notice the flat reference line in the plot representing this constant prediction across all sample points.

```rh-diagram
{"version":1,"diagram":{"title":"A constant mean baseline","caption":"Illustrative values; the geometry shows the stated relationship.","kind":"coordinate-plot","x":{"label":"Sample","min":0,"max":8},"y":{"label":"Target","min":0,"max":50},"series":[{"label":"Targets","kind":"scatter","points":[{"x":1,"y":25},{"x":2,"y":45},{"x":3,"y":39},{"x":4,"y":42},{"x":5,"y":35},{"x":6,"y":23},{"x":7,"y":43},{"x":8,"y":32}]}],"annotations":[{"kind":"reference-line","label":"Mean prediction of 35.5","axis":"y","value":35.5}]}}
```

Mathematically, this baseline minimizes the sum of squared errors. The formula for the mean is $\bar{y} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} y_i$, which yields a constant prediction.

Any complex machine learning model must beat the error rate of this simple average to prove its worth. If a regressor performs worse than predicting the mean, the features hold no useful predictive signal.

Each cell represents a specific combination of actual and predicted categories, separating correct guesses from errors.

Look at the values in the matrix below to trace how true conditions compare with what the model output.

Notice how the highest attention weights concentrate on specific contextual tokens rather than spreading evenly across the entire sentence.

```rh-diagram

In this unmasked example, the six weights from “sat” sum to 1.","kind":"token-links","source":["the","cat","sat","on","the","mat"],"target":["the","cat","sat","on","the","mat"],"queries":[{"index":2,"weights":[0.23,0.25,0.38,0.15,0.59,0.6]}],"normalized":true}}
```

The token sat places its heaviest emphasis on mat and the final context terms, capturing the structural and semantic relationships within the phrase.

These computed weights are normalized using the softmax function, ensuring that all outgoing scores from the query sum to one exactly.

title: Self-attention weights for sat
body:
When a model computes self-attention, each token compares itself to all other tokens in the context window. Look at how the token sat assigns attention weights across the phrase the cat sat on the mat.

```rh-diagram
{"version":1,"diagram":{"title":"How sat attends to the sentence","caption":"Thicker, darker arrows carry more weight. In this unmasked example, the six weights from sat sum to 1.","kind":"token-links","source":["the","cat","sat","on","the","mat"],"target":["the","cat","sat","on","the","mat"],"queries":[{"index":2,"weights":[0.09,0.07,0.59,0.03,0.08,0.14]}],"normalized":true}}
```

The query vector for sat computes a dot product with every key vector, yielding raw scores that are scaled and passed through a softmax function.

The highest weight points back to sat itself at 0.59, capturing its own semantic core.

Contextual linkage also connects sat to cat at 0.07 and mat at 0.14, establishing the subject and location of the action. These normalized weights sum to one, distributing the query's focus across the sequence.
